clue.text: South American city body almost accepting investment from American

indicators.note: the trimmed body takes in another letter, as if accepting it inside
almost means the word for body loses its final letter

parts.note: a carcass is a dead body
A is the abbreviation for American; 'investment' says it is put in, like a deposit

explanation.surface: A city's governing body nearly gets foreign capital from an American investor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts CARCASS to CARCAS, and 'accepting' takes A inside it. 'City body' looks like a council, but the body here is a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela, a South American country.

clue.text: Policeman about to enter river, pulling up ape

parts.note: cop is slang for policeman

indicators.note: in a down clue pulling up reads the letters from the bottom upward
the abbreviation goes into the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A policeman about to go into a river drags out an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts C into TAY, making TACY; 'pulling up' turns it to YCAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate them, as a copycat does; both are imitators.

clue.text: Cost of shaving accessory getting the bird?

indicators.note: 'cost of' puts the charge after the item it is for

parts.note: a razor is used to shave
a bill is the cost you have to pay

explanation.surface: Paying for a razor and getting a bird instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a whimsical invoice for a razor.
explanation.definitionFit: The razorbill is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family.

clue.text: Damage inappropriate to mention in Venice's unusual promotional activity

indicators.note: the damage and the inappropriate pieces are placed in the mixed-up city letters
unusual letters are an odd arrangement, so they are rearranged

parts.note: to harm is to damage
a remark that is off is improper or out of order

explanation.surface: Harm unsuitable to discuss during an odd Venetian publicity campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' scrambles the city's letters so that C lands in front and ENSIVE at the back, with the 'in' pieces between; the apostrophe in Venice's is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm offensive is a campaign of flattery and friendliness to win people over.

clue.text: Particular issue very much distracted them in Government

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so tired'

indicators.note: a distracted word is muddled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specific matter has ministers in government badly distracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distracted' rearranges THEM to METH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something, as in 'there's something I want to raise', refers to a particular but unnamed matter.

clue.text: See you mostly pay attention to Spanish river after beginning to cross

indicators.note: the beginning of a word means only its opening letter is taken
mostly means the phrase's word loses its final letter

parts.note: to heed is to pay attention
río is Spanish for river

explanation.surface: A farewell: you nearly listen to the Spanish river once you start to cross it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See you' looks like an instruction to look elsewhere, but it is the definition: a casual goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual British ways of saying goodbye, so the farewell phrase and the word are synonyms.

clue.text: Military officer in charge has stomach upset

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: An army officer in command has a bad stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, a stomach complaint.

clue.text: Lighthouse location implied to be sodden yet?

parts.note: the answer read as instructions, the first word with '...' as its anagram signal, gives these letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether a lighthouse site is wet yet.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read 'rocks' as an anagram signal and the first word scrambled gives SODDEN YET.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddystone reef off Plymouth in Devon carries a famous lighthouse.

clue.text: Uppity attitude about orange juice getting a stronger drink

indicators.note: the reversed attitude goes about, around, the juice
uppity in a down clue reads the word upward, from the bottom

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: A snooty drinker turns from orange juice to something stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uppity' reads as snobbish, but in a down clue it signals the word read upwards, giving RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red wine, stronger than juice.

clue.text: Heading away, perhaps June and I may be busy

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, is removed from the word

parts.note: June is an example of a month
the ego is the self, 'I'

explanation.surface: June and I, perhaps, are busy heading off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading away' drops M from MONTH; 'June' looks like a person but is an example of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone always on the move or active is described with this idiom for being busy.

clue.text: One article not available in form of square — this food is usually round

indicators.note: something not available is absent, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a piazza is an Italian town square
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wry joke that this round food comes in a square box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not available' removes one A from PIAZZA. The square/round contrast is the joke: pizzas are round but come in square boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pizza is a flat dish of dough with toppings, normally circular in shape.

clue.text: Notice French king tucking into whisky without much skill

indicators.note: the pair of pieces are placed inside the drink, as if eaten by it

parts.note: malt is malt whisky
an ad, advertisement, is a notice
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A French monarch clumsily knocks back whisky as an advert looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' is a noun here, an advertisement, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means clumsy or inept, lacking dexterity or skill.

clue.text: Tonal structure active in complex choral music etc, not universal

indicators.note: a complex arrangement means these letters are tangled into a new order
not universal tells the solver to strip the letter standing for universal from the mix

parts.note: A is the grammatical abbreviation for active (voice)
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A musical structure that is busy within elaborate choral music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' mixes A with CHORAL MUSIC ETC, and 'not universal' removes the U.
explanation.definitionFit: This series of all twelve semitones is a structure of tones used in music.

clue.text: See 11
Cheers one knockout Japanese drum

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
I is the Roman numeral one
KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout

explanation.surface: A drummer is thanked after one knockout performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' as thanks is British usage, here giving TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiko are large Japanese percussion instruments played with sticks.

clue.text: See 3
Confusion with men returning in horrible big limo

indicators.note: the reversed men sit in the middle of the jumbled car letters
something horrible is mangled, so these letters are rearranged
returning means the word read backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Chaos as soldiers come back in an ugly stretch limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' yields IMBGLIO from the car letters, and the turned-round men go in after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a complicated, embarrassing tangle of a situation.

clue.text: Source of electrons: gamble successfully handled, picked up over a year

indicators.note: in a down clue the reversed piece sits over, above, the rest

parts.note: to bet is to gamble

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means the word is lifted and read upward

parts.note: to ace something is to handle it successfully

explanation.surface: A winning bet, handled well, collected after a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' tempts as a sound signal, but in a down clue it is a reversal, giving DECA.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of radioactive decay emits electrons from atomic nuclei.

clue.text: Confusion of 'bail' and 'mail' involves special form of pronunciation

indicators.note: the confused letters wrap round, involving, the extra letter
confusion of the two words means their letters are muddled together

explanation.surface: Mixing up two similar-sounding words leads to a speech quirk.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the two words look like the topic, but they are simply the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Labialism is a way of articulating sounds using the lips.

clue.text: Ring about this aggressive approach to stock management?

definitions.text: Ring about this aggressive approach to stock management?

parts.words: Ring about this aggressive approach to stock management?
parts.note: a ring for cattle is a bullring, the arena; a 'bull' on the stock market is an aggressive buyer, so the fight is in the ring

explanation.surface: A question about a bullish trading strategy and the ring where it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock is both livestock and stock-market shares; the ring is the arena where it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The contest between matador and animal takes place in a bullring, a ring of cattle-style 'stock'.

clue.text: Snip rod once more, taking off top

parts.note: a bar is a rod

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: again means once more

explanation.surface: Cutting a rod again, trimming off its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off top' removes the A of AGAIN. 'Snip' looks like a verb about cutting; it is the British noun for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a snip is something cheap, a good-value purchase.

clue.text: Award held by Queen — item presented after a blaze?

indicators.note: the award sits inside the royal letters, held between them

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: The Queen presents an award to a firefighter after a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented' suggests an honours ceremony, but the definition is a glowing remnant left after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing coal remains in the ashes once a fire has burned down.

clue.text: People desperate to photograph sailor turning up on deck

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it
in a down clue turning up reads the word upward

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor
a pack of cards is a deck

explanation.surface: Photographers keen to snap a sailor who appears on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes TAR into RAT, above PACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat pack is a derogatory name for a crowd of tabloid photographers and journalists.

clue.text: Symbol of winter: bird with barer notes when shivering

indicators.note: shivering letters tremble out of their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird with scantier plumage shivers in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' rearranges BIRD, BARER and NOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: This red-breasted bird features on Christmas cards and is a familiar emblem of the British winter.

clue.text: Refuse to accept source of intelligence and intellect

indicators.note: the refuse takes the letter in, accepting it inside

parts.note: bran is the husk left over from grain, refuse

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Turning down intelligence and intellect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb; it is the noun, meaning chaff.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's brain is their mental capacity or intelligence.

clue.text: See 21
Irascible Republican lawyer in America

parts.note: atty is the American abbreviation for attorney

explanation.surface: A short-tempered Republican attorney in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for irritable or bad-tempered.

clue.text: See 6
A mad activist, displaying primitive behaviour

indicators.note: mad letters have lost order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild activist is behaving like a caveman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' gives TAVISTIC, which follows the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Atavistic behaviour reverts to that of remote ancestors, so it is primitive.

clue.text: Country's range of mountains, one further East

indicators.note: in an across entry east is the right, so the letter shifts further along to the right

parts.note: a mountain chain is a range
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A country with a mountain range, one lying further east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'further East' shifts the A of CHAIN to the right-hand end.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the most populous nation of East Asia.

clue.text: New military discipline ousting grand religious centre

indicators.note: ousting means the letter is expelled from the word

parts.note: gunnery is the military skill of operating guns
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A new army discipline replaces a grand religious establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting grand' removes G from GUNNERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent where nuns live is a religious community and centre.

clue.text: Veil military hospital gossip after switch of leaders

indicators.note: the leading letters of the two words change places

parts.note: MASH is a Mobile Army Surgical Hospital
to yak is to chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: Gossip at an army hospital about a veil.
explanation.walkthrough: MASH was popularised by the TV series of that name about a US army field hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is the face veil worn by some Muslim women.
